lessen.titel: Take a unit or two of chaff so you are not left without strategic pieces
lessen.tekst: An army of only damage dealers and casters leaves you little to do, and your opponent gets to dictate the tempo. A unit or two of chaff lets you disrupt his plans and enables your powerful units.
lessen.waarom: He found that armies made only of death stars, dragons, damage dealers and casters left him with little to do on the table. Chaff lets you interfere with the opponent's plans and enables your powerful units, and it often costs under 100 points. He also finds it makes the game more strategic, so you feel more like a general.
lessen.wanneerNiet: He cautions against spending too many points on chaff: these units support the fighting block, which still has to do the work.

bronnen.citaat: you get to stuff with your opponent's plans

extraCitaten.citaat: these units are costing you under 100 points

bronnen.citaat: one or two pieces tends to be pretty good.

lessen.titel: Use speed bumps to pull enemy units out of position
lessen.tekst: A speed bump redirects enemy units by getting in the way, so they charge it or cannot get around it. It is there to die, but to die while achieving something.
lessen.waarom: It all comes down to wasting your opponent's time: getting in the way forces him into decisions he did not expect or want to make. Part of a list's win condition can be that this unit moves an enemy out of position so it cannot perform at its peak. Redirecting is difficult, but he thinks mastering it makes you a top tier player.
lessen.voorbeeld: He put a Great Eagle in front of Grail Knights that threatened his Waywatchers and Wild Riders. The knights had to charge and kill the eagle, overran in the direction he chose, and his Wild Riders could later charge them without being countercharged and win that flank.

bronnen.citaat: their main function is to redirect things and move enemy units out of position
Sometimes its job is simply to stand in the way.
They're very good at redirecting charges.

lessen.titel: Decoys with kill potential draw resources away from your real threats
lessen.tekst: Fast, dangerous chaff that threatens backline units like artillery or light cavalry cannot be ignored. While your opponent spends shooting and units on it, he is not dealing with your bigger threats.
lessen.waarom: Decoys are fast and dangerous, so if left alone they threaten backline units such as artillery and light cavalry, or become a flanking force that turns a key combat. Dealing with them costs the opponent resources and buys time for your win condition. He likes them most because they do not just take up space: they threaten a space and force a response.
lessen.voorbeeld: An enemy Helblaster Volley Gun shooting a 95 point Mangler Squig is not shooting your big unit of Boar Boyz. He names the Mangler Squig as his favourite decoy and a Hell Pit as an expensive version that works the same way.

bronnen.citaat: Your opponent has to pour resources into dealing with them.
you have to kill it or be killed by it.
spells so good that he can't just leave my Chariot out there doing nothing

lessen.titel: Use cheap units as early deployment drops
lessen.tekst: Without chaff you end up putting your key units down early, before your opponent. Cheap drops force him to commit his units first, so you can react and place your win conditions in the matchups you want.
lessen.waarom: If every unit in your list must perform to win, you end up dropping your key pieces first, and that alone shapes the game. When the opponent places his big flanking unit before your counter unit, he has committed to a flank and you can react. Scouts also gain intel during deployment.
lessen.voorbeeld: Wood Elf Beast Packs, a handler and two beasts for about 30 points, are in his view the best scout unit in the game. Giant Rats at 30 points without a handler do the same, and in marching column they become a speed bump.
lessen.wanneerNiet: He says extra cheap drops can be wasted on armies that really want to go first and therefore prefer as few deployment drops as possible.

bronnen.citaat: If you don't have chaff in deployment, you're often dropping your key pieces down early
You can deploy these units early to give yourself more drops than your opponent.
It allows you to waste drops

lessen.titel: Chaff must be fast or mobile
lessen.tekst: Chaff has to get into position ahead of the enemy, so it needs high movement or mobility such as fly, skirmish or reserve move. For a speed bump the speaker wants fly or movement seven as a minimum.
lessen.waarom: Chaff is about getting into position ahead of the opponent; too slow and it cannot get in the way or into the right spot to flee in the direction you want. He separates speed (high movement) from mobility (skirmish, fly, reserve move), which lets chaff use every corner of the board.
lessen.voorbeeld: His checklist: under 100 points and movement seven or more, with fly, skirmish or reserve move as bonuses. For a speed bump he wants fly and movement seven as a minimum.

bronnen.citaat: needs to be fast because it's about getting them in position ahead of your opponent
they need to be fast
have enough move to orient your base in a way

lessen.titel: Keep chaff cheap, roughly under 100 points
lessen.tekst: Chaff is likely to die, so it should be cheap; the speaker uses about 100 points as the threshold. A unit above that has to give a good return to be worth it.
lessen.waarom: Chaff has to go into dangerous parts of the board, so it is likely to die and the return shrinks as it gets more expensive. He credits an early Wood Elf guide by AJ of the Rank and Flank podcast for the under 100 points threshold and thinks it still holds.
lessen.voorbeeld: For elves, a unit of seven Dryads with a Nymph at about 120 points can still be chaff, because chaff is defined by what it is trying to do.
lessen.wanneerNiet: Some armies can go over 100 points, but then the unit has to give a good return.

bronnen.citaat: get a good return back from a unit that is over 100 points
generally cheap is under 100 points for the unit.
less than 100 points open order or close order diverters

lessen.titel: The best chaff covers several roles, but give each unit a specific job
lessen.tekst: Chaff that can fulfil multiple roles is the best kind: Giant Rats can be a cheap scout drop and a speed bump, and a Great Eagle can redirect and still kill a war machine. Each chaff unit should still go in the list for a specific role.
lessen.waarom: Chaff shines when it can fulfil more than one role, but each unit should still go in the list as the time waster for a specific role.
lessen.voorbeeld: Giant Rats are a scout just by being cheap and placed early, and a speed bump because they are fast and their formation lets you control how units contact them. The Great Eagle is there to redirect with its close order, yet with three or four attacks, a stomp, strength four and weapon skill five it can also kill a war machine.

bronnen.citaat: If they can fulfill multiple roles they are S tier chaff unit.

extraCitaten.citaat: So, they can go and kill a war machine.

bronnen.citaat: at the start of the game you have to have a role for these units.

lessen.titel: Mangler Squigs make a strong decoy on a flank
lessen.tekst: With a 3D6 random move the opponent has to respect an 11 to 12 inch threat in any direction. Placed on a flank opposite something like Chaos Knights, they make the knights hold back and delay their push into your backline.
lessen.waarom: He sees Mangler Squigs as chaff and the perfect decoy: a 3D6 random move, strength six impact hits, killing blow, stomps and random attacks give huge damage potential. The threat makes the opponent change how he moves, and with toughness five and four wounds they may win the combat if they get to hit back.
lessen.voorbeeld: Rangers were shooting him while pushing down his right flank. He moved his Manglers into range until one could hit them; over two or three combats they killed the whole unit without losing a Mangler, and soaked up the arrows in the meantime.
lessen.wanneerNiet: The random move can also come up short, as low as four inches, and they have to wheel.

bronnen.citaat: has to respect an 11 to 12 in any direction

extraCitaten.citaat: So, it manipulates what your opponent does because of its threat.

bronnen.citaat: a mangler is chaff, but I do believe it is.

lessen.titel: Use light chariots as decoys and artillery hunters
lessen.tekst: A Goblin Wolf Chariot is fast and its impact hits threaten lightly armoured units such as Outriders and artillery. Pushed forward, it cannot be ignored, which buys time for your main units.
lessen.waarom: Light chariots are good decoys and also good speed bumps. They cannot be ignored because their impact hits can kill Outriders, which opponents like to protect. A Goblin Wolf Chariot is very fast with swift stride, and artillery has little armour, so its impact hits are a real threat.
lessen.voorbeeld: In his Nomadic Waaagh list one chariot pushed forward to pressure Outriders and bait the Demigryph Knights, buying his Wyvern a turn. Another stood beside his Boar Boyz to shape a Griffon's charge; when the Griffon charged the Boar Boyz instead, the chariot roamed free and smashed a mortar in one turn.

bronnen.citaat: Wolf chariots are great artillery hunters.

extraCitaten.citaat: he gets into a mortar and smashes it in one turn

bronnen.citaat: the Goblin Wolf chariot also I believe really great use of chaff.

lessen.titel: A decoy wins either way: killed late or left free
lessen.tekst: The job of a decoy is not to die but to make your opponent choose between wasting time killing it and letting it run free to do its job.
lessen.waarom: If you do not deal with a decoy it has something to do, so it is not just there to die. He notes that opponents often decide to go and kill it anyway.

bronnen.citaat: The job is to make your opponent decide whether to waste time killing it
Their sole role isn't to die

extraCitaten.citaat: your opponent's not going to let their great cannon die.

lessen.titel: A speed bump must be close or open order, not skirmishers
lessen.tekst: A charging unit has to align to the front of a close or open order speed bump, so when it wins it overruns in a direction you chose, for example away from the flank of your main unit. Skirmishers cannot steer the post-combat movement this way; the speaker thinks a Great Eagle is the best unit for it.
lessen.waarom: A speed bump takes a hit, dies and shapes the post combat movement. With close or open order the charger has to align to its front, so when it wins it overruns in a direction that protects your other units, and you may countercharge the unit that got sucked in (Chaff video). Against a close order Great Eagle the charger either takes a restraint test and stays put for the turn, or overruns in the direction you chose (Flanks video).
lessen.voorbeeld: Skin Wolves charged his open order Goblin Wolf Riders, killed them and overran in a direction that protected the flank of his Boar Boyz. He adds that a Boar Chariot wheeled a little further could then have countercharged the Skin Wolves (Chaff video).
lessen.wanneerNiet: Skirmishers can still pull a unit where you want if it is frenzied or you are its only possible charge target, but they cannot shape the post combat move this way.

bronnen.citaat: being a speed bump is non-negotiable. It cannot be a skirmish unit
It has close order, so the opponent has to align to it.
most importantly they're non skirmishers.

lessen.titel: When frenzy baiting, be the only unit they can redirect to
lessen.tekst: A fast speed bump can sit at the edge of a frenzied unit's charge range, take the charge, flee and rally. Make sure there is nothing else for the enemy to redirect into, or the bait is wasted.
lessen.waarom: A speed bump with swift stride is his main frenzy bait: it can sit at the very edge of a frenzied unit's charge range, make it charge, then flee and try to rally. If the enemy can redirect into something else after you flee, the whole move was a waste of time.
lessen.voorbeeld: He calls a Razorgor a very good speed bump and decoy for this.

bronnen.citaat: make sure it's the only unit there that's going to get charged

extraCitaten.citaat: at the very edge of a frenzied unit's charge distance, make them charge you

lessen.titel: Think of the board in thirds and aim to win two of them
lessen.tekst: Plan your game as left flank, centre and right flank. You do not need to win all three: winning two thirds of the board generally wins the game.
lessen.waarom: It is the overarching principle: deployment ties the flanks and the centre together, and what you do afterwards decides whether you roll into the middle or the backline and own space. You do not need to win all three thirds.
lessen.voorbeeld: Two thirds can be the centre and one flank, or both flanks, after which you overwhelm the centre with a bigger flanking force than the enemy has left there.
lessen.wanneerNiet: He frames this as a principle for balanced games and notes that a massive list disparity can allow one army to win all three thirds.

bronnen.citaat: you need to think of the game or the board of three/3s

extraCitaten.citaat: if you win two/ird of the board, then you're generally going to win the

bronnen.citaat: If you win two out of three of them, generally you win the game.

lessen.titel: Most armies hold the centre, win the flanks, then overwhelm the centre
lessen.tekst: About 80 percent of armies rely on a heavy anvil in the middle. Winning a flank is usually not enough on its own; the point is to free your flank units to turn on the centre later.
lessen.waarom: Faster units sit on the flanks, so the action starts there early, while the centre becomes a standoff about who holds longest. If your flank units do not get unlocked you cannot win the centre. Flank matchups are rarely one sided, so you often sacrifice something to win one.
lessen.voorbeeld: Against Alex's Beastmen his block of Black Orcs with a Shaman and battle standard, about 700 points, held the centre. His stacked right flank won, then his Squig Hoppers and Wolf Riders charged into the central combat and turned it.
lessen.wanneerNiet: With Wood Elves, which he also plays, he thinks you win by winning the flanks and creating space, because winning the centre alone is very hard.

bronnen.citaat: hold the center, win the flanks, overwhelm the center later
the central unit needs to buy time, take a hit, fall back,
destroy his flanking force and

lessen.titel: On a flank you either kill things or waste time
lessen.tekst: Put units that can hit hard on the flank you mean to win, and use chaff to delay the enemy on the other one. Both are valid ways to play a flank.
lessen.waarom: You need units that can hit things to destroy the enemy on one flank, and chaff to delay the enemy on the other. He calls that split the key to getting the most out of flank units.
lessen.voorbeeld: His skirmishing characters, frenzied Boar Boyz and Squig Hoppers did the killing on his right, while Goblin Wolf Riders on his left used feigned flight to draw a charge and get away.

bronnen.citaat: to kill things, but sometimes you just want to waste time

extraCitaten.citaat: their role was to draw in a charge, get out of there

bronnen.citaat: maybe a weak flank or distracting a unit

lessen.titel: Do not just park heavy cavalry on a flank and charge the closest target
lessen.tekst: A five-wide unit of knights on the flank charging whatever comes closest is a misconception. Pick your fights in deployment and support your hammer with chaff such as wolf riders.
lessen.waarom: Once your hammer is on the flank it needs support from units like wolf riders. Simply placing a great flank unit such as Wild Riders at the edge of your deployment and sending it off does not work, and neither does parking a Heavy Chariot on a flank just because it does nothing in the middle.

bronnen.citaat: It's not that simple. You need to pick your fights through deployment

extraCitaten.citaat: you really need to invest in your flanks

lessen.titel: Judge a flank by who benefited, not by units lost
lessen.tekst: The speaker lost more points on one flank but still counts it as won, because his chaff bought the time he needed elsewhere. What happened on the flank and who gained from it matters more than the kill count.
lessen.waarom: Delaying the enemy on one flank can buy the time you need to win elsewhere. His Wolf Riders baited a charge and escaped, which bought a turn, then beat an infantry unit and came into the middle while the enemy Preyton was busy with his Boar Chariot.
lessen.voorbeeld: He lost the Boar Chariot and the Doom Diver on that flank, about 190 points, but it took his opponent longer than planned, which gave him time to win the right flank and the middle.

bronnen.citaat: think about winning a flank as not just killing more units than your opponent
I don't get his points, but I've won the time there.

lessen.titel: Combat infantry is too slow to win flanks
lessen.tekst: A good flank unit has speed, damage and durability. Infantry at movement four or five cannot compete with light or heavy cavalry out there; its strength is holding space in the centre.
lessen.waarom: Infantry's power is holding space and combat resolution. Its big drawback is speed: movement four, or five for elves and rats, cannot compete with light cavalry outmanoeuvring you or heavy cavalry picking its charge.
lessen.voorbeeld: In his game his Night Goblins stood on the left flank but faced the centre, because that is where they would be needed.

bronnen.citaat: I don't think you can really win flanks with infantry

extraCitaten.citaat: And their big disadvantage is they are slow.

lessen.titel: Give your hammers the speed to get the charge
lessen.tekst: Hammers are rarely effective when they are not charging. Look for high movement (seven or more, or six with swift stride), swift stride and countercharge so your hammer gets the charge it wants.
lessen.waarom: Charging is vital for winning combats on the flank, so he counts heavy cavalry as fast enough from about movement six with swift stride (Flanks video). Hammers are rarely effective when not charging; swift stride, countercharge and skirmish give redundancy, so you still get the matchup you want whatever happens on the table (Infantry video).
lessen.voorbeeld: Demigryph Knights have movement seven and swift stride, a 16 inch charge range, and countercharge lets them still charge back when out of position (Infantry video). Glade Riders with movement nine and reserve move use their speed to distract rather than to deal damage (Flanks video).
lessen.wanneerNiet: Speed is about what the unit does with it, not only the raw number (Flanks video).

bronnen.citaat: swift stride is a key thing because charging is vital for winning combats

extraCitaten.citaat: So speed needs to be thought of more than just a raw number

bronnen.citaat: it's very rare that they are effective if they are not charging

lessen.titel: Keep heavy cavalry and other hammers on the flanks, not in the centre
lessen.tekst: In the middle of the board hammers tend to get shot by everything. On the flanks you can use terrain to block line of sight and screen them with chaff until they can strike.
lessen.waarom: On the flanks a hammer can manoeuvre around terrain, use it to block line of sight from shooters, and be covered by screening skirmishers or chaff. In the middle, because of the terrain rule for the centre of the board, hammers tend to get blown up straight away. From the flanks they can later turn to the centre or get into the backline.
lessen.voorbeeld: He approves of his opponent placing a Tuskgor Chariot on the extreme flank.

bronnen.citaat: don't want to put a unit of heavy cav in the middle of the board
hard to have your hammers in the middle because they tend to just get shot
out on the extreme flank, I think you've got the right idea.

lessen.titel: Hammers need some durability because they will be targeted
lessen.tekst: Your opponent wants to kill your hammers first, so they need some redundancy: toughness four or more and at least a 3+ save, a 2+ preferred on heavy cavalry. Then they survive long enough to deal their damage.
lessen.waarom: Hammers win games, so the opponent targets them and they are often the first thing shot. If a hammer does not strike first in combat it is wasted; durability gives it redundancy to take a hit and still deal its damage.
lessen.voorbeeld: Wild Riders have no durability and get smashed by toughness four, 2+ save, multi wound Demigryph Knights if they fail to kill in the first round (Infantry video). Orc Boar Boyz with toughness four, a 5+ save and a 6+ ward will not go down to light shooting (Flanks video).

bronnen.citaat: You need some redundancy of toughness four or above a three up at least save
the reason they need durability is because your opponent wants to kill your hammers

lessen.titel: Put a mobile wizard on the flank, away from the dispel bubble
lessen.tekst: Opponents usually keep their wizard in the middle for a big dispel range. A reserve-move or flying caster on the flank can move out of that range, cast, and drop back to safety.
lessen.waarom: If the enemy pulls his own wizard out to the side to deal with yours, you have already won part of the mind game, and your caster is probably the more manoeuvrable one.
lessen.voorbeeld: A Renegade Crowns outcast wizard with Dark Magic cast his hex and enchantment, then used reserve move to drop out of dispel range, cast Doombolt and go back to safety. He mentions Pegasus riders, with versions in Dark Elves and Empire, and the Wood Elf Warhawk and reserve move Spellweaver.

bronnen.citaat: you can use their maneuverability to get out of your opponent's dispel range

lessen.titel: Skirmishing combat characters excel on the flanks
lessen.tekst: A skirmishing combat character can pick off targets or join your flank unit in a combat. Its 360 degree line of sight for charging gives it the flexibility to choose its fight.
lessen.waarom: With skirmish and a high charge distance it can pick things off and join combats you can compound, with the choice to commit alongside your flank unit or pick another target. He says such characters sway the course of the battle for about 250 to 300 points.
lessen.voorbeeld: His Orc War Boss on boar fought next to his Boar Boyz on the flank. He also uses a Great Stag version at about 280 to 300 points.
lessen.wanneerNiet: He thinks these characters probably lack the power to defeat a central block relying on combat resolution on their own.

extraCitaten.citaat: they only tend to cost about 300 points

lessen.titel: Screen hammers with cheap chaff that clears itself out of the way
lessen.tekst: Expendable chaff or a skirmishing screen gives cover to the unit behind it. When it needs to get out of the way, it charges something and sacrifices itself, and your hammer goes in.
lessen.waarom: A great flank unit placed at the edge of deployment and sent off does not work; the flank needs investment, and a screen protects your hammer until it picks its target.
lessen.voorbeeld: Wood Elf Beast Packs live on the flank and cover Wild Riders; once the screen gets out of the way, the Wild Riders pick their target and charge. Chaos Warhounds are another example of expendable chaff.

bronnen.citaat: When they need to get out of the way, they just charge something
A cheap disposable unit in front of your real damage dealer
So you just plunk an eagle in front of your high priority target.

lessen.titel: Sacrificing a flank is fine if you gain from it
lessen.tekst: Double down on the flank you want to win and use chaff to waste time on the one you expect to lose. The speaker accepts forfeiting a flank, but only when it buys something elsewhere.
lessen.waarom: You win a flank by doubling down on it and using chaff to waste time on the flank you expect to lose (Flanks video). A Heavy Chariot parked on a flank only because it does nothing in the middle sacrifices that flank for no gain.
lessen.voorbeeld: Against Empire he effectively gave up his left flank after a deployment mistake, but won his right flank heavily and broke through the middle; the game was a draw. Against Bretonnia an Eagle and Wildwood Rangers held one flank almost alone and drew fire that helped his main units break through (Deploy video).
lessen.wanneerNiet: Against Empire he thinks he went too heavy on one flank and should have left something on the other side (Deploy video).

bronnen.citaat: It's fine to sacrifice things and indeed fine to sacrifice an entire flank
I'm a big fan of forfeiting a flank
willingly sacrificing a third is also a pretty strong strategy.

lessen.titel: Terror is a powerful tool on the flanks
lessen.tekst: On a flank the enemy is away from his general and close to the board edge, so a unit that flees from terror takes turns to get back, if it returns at all. A cheap character with a faction item that grants terror can do this too.
lessen.waarom: Making an opponent flee is a huge deal: even if the unit rallies, it takes many turns to get back to the centre. Monsters already suit the flanks with high toughness, mobility, stomps and impact hits, so one that causes terror is even better.
lessen.voorbeeld: His Arachnarok Spider caused terror in a Leadership 9 Renegade Crowns sellsword unit; it fled, lost its warband bonus and ran off the board, 160 points gone, and he turned into the middle. He also mentions a Wood Elf banner that gives fear, which lets Wild Riders cause terror.

bronnen.citaat: Terror is such a powerful tool on the flanks

extraCitaten.citaat: it's going to take them like four turns to get back into the center

lessen.titel: Once a flank is won, turn into the centre or the backline
lessen.tekst: Winning a flank opens up space. Use it to push into the backline against war machines and wizards, or turn into the centre and flank charge the units holding it.
lessen.waarom: Your flank units should support the rest of the board, while the units in the centre do the dirty work of holding it.
lessen.voorbeeld: After his Arachnarok Spider won its flank, it turned and drove straight through the middle of the board.

bronnen.citaat: And when you win the flank, you open up space for you to play in.
your shabi are free to are free to wheel this way. Move up.
cut back across into the middle from the rear.

lessen.titel: A hammer first of all has to deal damage
lessen.tekst: Hitting power is the most important part of a hammer: many attacks, high strength, armour piercing, stomps or impact hits. Durability and mobility come after that.
lessen.waarom: The hammer is the unit that breaks the enemy while the anvil holds it in place. Whatever the unit type, dealing damage is the first and most important job.
lessen.voorbeeld: Wild Riders have zero durability, but on the charge they get three attacks each at strength five with AP2 and armour bane, which makes up for it.

bronnen.citaat: what it needs to do is deal damage

extraCitaten.citaat: The anvil holds them in place

lessen.titel: Send each hammer into the matchup it wins
lessen.tekst: Wild Riders do well into infantry but come out second best against heavily armoured heavy cavalry. A hammer that underperforms may simply be in the wrong matchup, which you set up at deployment and with chaff.
lessen.waarom: He sees matchups as about 80 percent of the game. They are decided at deployment or by enabling your hammers with chaff, screens and buffs.
lessen.voorbeeld: Wild Riders kill enough infantry without being hit back, but against Demigryph Knights with a 2+ save, toughness four and multiple wounds they get smashed if they do not kill in the first round.

bronnen.citaat: You might just be sending it into the wrong matchup

extraCitaten.citaat: which matchups to me is probably 80% of the game

lessen.titel: Behemoths make good hammers on the flanks
lessen.tekst: Stomps give them reliable damage, and terror means a unit that loses to them is more likely to flee instead of falling back in good order. Most behemoths can stomp their way out of a bad engagement.
lessen.waarom: Behemoths can wreck both infantry and heavy cavalry through high strength and AP2 thunder stomps, and they often have five or more high strength attacks with good AP.
lessen.voorbeeld: A Giant Spawn of Chaos rolling a six on its stomps will cook Wild Riders and even hurt Demigryph Knights with strength six AP2 hits.

bronnen.citaat: likely to make that unit flee as opposed to just fall back in good order

extraCitaten.citaat: mainly because of their high strength and their thunder stomps

lessen.titel: Use heavy chariots as support pieces, not as your main hammer
lessen.tekst: Put something in front that holds and falls back in good order, then countercharge with the chariot to get its impact hits in. The speaker would not recommend heavy chariots to new players.
lessen.waarom: When they connect, heavy chariots are devastating through their impact hits. But the first charge bonus is easily wasted, they are easy to kill with only four wounds and hard to get into position, and impact hits can spike but are never certain.
lessen.voorbeeld: D6+1 impact hits at strength five AP2 can wreck a unit of infantry.
lessen.wanneerNiet: He would not recommend them to new players, who are likely to be disappointed.

bronnen.citaat: I like to think of them as support pieces though rather than your main hammer

extraCitaten.citaat: It's very easy to kill. It's hard to get into position.

lessen.titel: Infantry can hold and kill if it keeps armour piercing while parrying
lessen.tekst: A hybrid hammer has some static combat resolution and durability but also high quality attacks, so it kills models when it is charged. It needs weapons that still give armour piercing when parrying, such as the speaker describes for Chaos Warriors and Stormvermin.
lessen.waarom: He finds units that are only immovable boring; a hybrid brings static combat resolution and durability but kills models when it hits back, so the opponent is invited to come for the points and can be punished. Being able to parry and still hit with armour piercing is a massive deal.
lessen.voorbeeld: Chaos Warriors with ensorcelled weapons are strength four AP1 with a 3+ save in combat. Stormvermin with halberds can parry for a 3+ save and hit back at AP1, or use the halberds for AP2 on the charge.
lessen.wanneerNiet: He does not think all elite infantry can do this and doubts Swordmasters get a look in.

lessen.titel: Run Black Orcs with great weapons, two ranks deep
lessen.tekst: Black Orcs with great weapons hit back with strength six AP2 attacks even when charged, and stubborn keeps them in place. The speaker now builds them as 14 models, two ranks, all great weapons.
lessen.waarom: Black Orcs are toughness four, base strength four and stubborn, so they hold while nearby units countercharge, and with press of battle they hit back with many strength six AP2 attacks. He no longer likes to parry with them.
lessen.voorbeeld: A big unit of Chaos Knights charged his 14 Black Orcs: he lost two and killed three in return. The combat tied, the knights lost their lance bonus the next turn and the Black Orcs cleaned house.

lessen.titel: Build a Stormvermin brick ten wide with swift stride
lessen.tekst: The speaker runs 26 to 28 Stormvermin with a Warlord and a battle standard bearer carrying the swift stride banner, ten wide to maximise attacks rather than as a horde. The swift stride lets the infantry be the aggressor.
lessen.waarom: The swift stride banner gives movement five infantry a long charge, which unlocks the power of infantry. He goes ten wide because it is more fun and gets good results, and keeps about six or seven static combat resolution plus the Grand Banner of Superiority.
lessen.voorbeeld: His Stormvermin charged foot Knights of the Realm with great weapons and killed eight in the first round, about 15 combat resolution in total. Over three rounds they destroyed the unit and broke through the centre.

lessen.titel: A behemoth that holds and kills needs unbreakable
lessen.tekst: A behemoth with an offensive package and unbreakable can run into infantry, lose on combat resolution and still not break, while taking models out with stomps and attacks. The speaker's example is the Hell Pit Abomination.
lessen.waarom: Behemoths tend to have an offensive package anyway; unbreakable lets them hold up a lot, so they can lose on combat resolution and still have taken models out.
lessen.voorbeeld: He has held up a monster slaying Duke with a Hell Pit. He thinks the new Gargantuan treeman may also fit, because it can cast, has a decent number of attacks and stomps, and is unbreakable.
lessen.wanneerNiet: A Gigantic Spawn has potential but is more an anvil than a hammer: the unit needs real offensive power, not just to be a roadblock.

lessen.titel: Hybrid hammer units are good objective holders
lessen.tekst: A unit that can sit on an objective and still kill whatever comes to take it has a role in the scoring game. Making such a unit core is another benefit.
lessen.waarom: Such a unit keeps the death star role of come and get me while it holds an objective, but it can kill you if you come and fail. That gives it a role on the board.
lessen.voorbeeld: He describes moving Chaos Knights onto an objective early, then leaving them there to score while Countercharge makes the opponent cautious about attacking.

lessen.titel: Before deploying, work out who is the beatdown
lessen.tekst: Decide whose list is the aggressor. Aggression can also be firepower, like a gunline or an alpha strike that tries to cripple you in turns one and two.
lessen.waarom: The term comes from Magic: the Gathering and is about tempo: some armies need to win early, others win in the late game. List building freedom, especially with armies of infamy, lets you steer toward an aggressive, control or mixed arms army.
lessen.voorbeeld: City-State of Nuln lists with heavy firepower, and Cathay with its alpha strike, try to wreck you in turns one and two; if you survive that, you have a good chance.

bronnen.citaat: consider who is the beatdown
who has to make the move is probably Chris
Are you the aggressor? If so, go hard.

lessen.titel: Use the terrain you see before deployment to place key units
lessen.tekst: Terrain is visible before anything is placed, so it gives you key locations, such as a hill for a cannon or ranged unit. Wood Elves can extend impassable terrain with their woodland ambush to create a line of sight blocker.
lessen.waarom: In his opinion terrain is where the skill in deployment comes from, because it shows key locations before you see where the enemy deploys.
lessen.voorbeeld: With Wood Elves he connects his woodland ambush forest to impassable terrain or a hill almost every game to create more space to hide. A cannon or ranged unit often goes on a hill to see the whole battlefield.

bronnen.citaat: You get to see that before you put your first model down.
identify what each important piece of terrain is doing.
look at what's in front of you and see what affects the game.

lessen.titel: A slow army should not deploy too spread out
lessen.tekst: If you are the slow army you risk being drawn around the board all game. Consider closing in on one corner and locking down part of the enemy army instead.
lessen.waarom: Speed is about board control and space. Instead of spreading out, a slow army can close in on one corner and lock down part of the enemy army while its more flexible pieces pick off chaff.
lessen.voorbeeld: Dwarfs are always the slow army; movement three limits what they can do, even with marching column and drilled.

bronnen.citaat: if you are the slow army, you don't want to deploy too spread out

extraCitaten.citaat: They're always the slow army.

lessen.titel: Deploy your units opposite the enemy units they beat
lessen.tekst: Often all it takes is putting your heavy cavalry opposite enemy heavy cavalry it will beat. The speaker deployed his win condition unit after the enemy unit it needed to kill.
lessen.waarom: Your win condition unit needs to take out a key enemy unit; if it does, your chances increase significantly.
lessen.voorbeeld: Against Empire, his Wild Riders with a Glade Lord were about the only unit that could kill toughness four, 2+ save Demigryph Knights, so he dropped them after the Demigryphs. Against Bretonnia his Wild Riders and Great Stag lined up on the Grail Knights, a unit worth about 500 points.
lessen.wanneerNiet: He says a development that forces a rethink can justify changing the planned matchups.

I need to match them up across from those things that I've chosen

lessen.titel: In King of the Hill you can give up the hill early
lessen.tekst: The speaker let his opponent take the hill in the early game so the enemy had to come forward. Units on a hill have a hard time avoiding charges, so he planned combo charges on it around turn three or four.
lessen.waarom: With Wood Elves, and Wild Hunt in particular, he finds it hard to hold the hill from turn one to six, so letting the opponent have it makes the enemy come forward.
lessen.voorbeeld: Later his Glade Riders scooted round to capture the hill and used it to block line of sight.

extraCitaten.citaat: it's extremely hard to avoid charges when you're sitting on a hill

lessen.titel: Against heavy shooting, deploy fragile units defensively
lessen.tekst: Units deployed forward that cannot charge on turn one just give enemy cannons and shooters targets. With Wood Elves the speaker says to deploy defensively and keep out of sight.
lessen.waarom: The enemy Outriders' early presence and firepower made the Empire player the beatdown: going first, he could unload a volley and weaken the Wood Elves badly before combat.
lessen.voorbeeld: He placed units forward on his left flank; the opponent shot two Warhawk Riders dead with a cannon and shot his Wildwood Rangers with the Outriders. Deployed further back, the cannons would have had nothing to shoot.
lessen.wanneerNiet: Against an army with little shooting, while going first, he deployed more aggressively.

use this forest to block line of sight to some high priority targets
I had to whittle down uh his range shooting and deploy defensively

lessen.titel: Deploy more aggressively when there is little shooting and you go first
lessen.tekst: Against an army with little shooting, and knowing he would get the first turn, the speaker had the freedom to deploy further forward and put pressure on his opponent from turn one.
lessen.waarom: The Bretonnian army had more combat units and little shooting, only Peasant Bowmen and a Trebuchet, and since Bretonnia always prays he knew he would go first. That let him set up his first turn and put pressure on his opponent.
lessen.voorbeeld: He pushed up aggressively but kept everything out of the Duke's charge range, and lined up his Wild Riders and Great Stag to charge the Grail Knights.

lessen.titel: Check the scenario and deployment map before placing units
lessen.tekst: Before deploying, check which scenario you are playing and what shape your deployment zone has. Account for whether it gives your army a wide area or confines it to a narrower space.
lessen.waarom: He says different deployment maps can completely change how an army approaches the game.
lessen.voorbeeld: He starts by examining Encirclement's deployment restrictions and the positions of the three strategic objectives.

bronnen.citaat: First, know the scenario.

lessen.titel: Identify which objectives your army can realistically contest
lessen.tekst: Before deployment, check how many objectives there are and where they are. Decide which ones your army can realistically contest.
lessen.waarom: He says an objective on the other side of the battlefield might not be relevant to your army at all.
lessen.voorbeeld: In his two-tower game, core infantry of unit strength 10 or more could capture the objectives, so he considered his Night Goblins and Black Orcs for the towers.
lessen.wanneerNiet: He says ignoring objectives might work if a severe list disparity lets you wipe out the opposing army.

deploy in a way that means you can contest, capture, or hold objectives

lessen.titel: Ask which enemy units fly or have Swiftstride
lessen.tekst: Before deployment, ask which enemy units can fly or have Swiftstride. Track where those units are placed and account for their threat ranges when deploying valuable units.
lessen.waarom: He says these abilities can create enormous threat ranges, so a valuable unit may be unsafe even when you think it is far enough away.

lessen.titel: Locate enemy magic threats before positioning your wizard
lessen.tekst: Ask which enemy models are wizards and which have bound spells or bound magic items. Use the positions of those threats to decide where to deploy your own wizard so it can attempt to stop enemy spells.

lessen.tekst: Before deploying, ask whether your opponent has ambushers and whether any will actually ambush. Account for threats that will arrive later instead of considering only the units placed during deployment.

lessen.titel: Check for scouts and vanguard before judging positions safe
lessen.tekst: Ask whether your opponent has scouts or vanguard units before you finish deploying. Account for how much closer those units could start when deciding whether a position is safe.

lessen.titel: Consider fewer drops when the first turn matters
lessen.tekst: If the scenario offers a first-turn roll bonus for finishing deployment first, consider reducing your deployment drops. He suggests this particularly for a fast, aggressive army that places high value on going first.
lessen.waarom: He says getting the first turn can be extremely valuable for a fast, aggressive army.
lessen.wanneerNiet: He says more drops give more information and control over the final deployment. The choice depends on your army, the scenario and how important the first turn is.

bronnen.citaat: you may want to minimize the number of drops

extraCitaten.citaat: More drops give you more information and more control over the final deployment.

lessen.titel: Deploy for the position you want in later turns
lessen.tekst: Deploy your army around a shared plan for where its units should be over the next two or three turns. Before pursuing a quick charge, consider the position after the combat and whether the unit will still have support.
lessen.waarom: He says getting one unit into combat quickly is not necessarily a victory. A slightly passive deployment can force the opponent to make the first difficult decision.

lessen.titel: Consider central deployment against cavalry threatening your flank

lessen.titel: Concentrate force against only part of the enemy army
lessen.tekst: Concentrate your units to create a local advantage rather than spreading them evenly into equal fights. You can leave part of the battlefield empty while concentrating your strength elsewhere.
lessen.waarom: He argues that you do not necessarily need a better army if more of yours fights the right part of theirs.

lessen.titel: Check that deployment leaves useful first-turn movement choices
lessen.tekst: Before accepting your deployment, check whether you can advance, hold, threaten a charge, redirect or respond to your opponent on the first movement phase. Reconsider the deployment if you cannot identify useful options.
lessen.waarom: He describes bad positioning as leaving every possible move with a problem.

lessen.titel: Place skirmishing chaff behind your block as a retreat backstop
lessen.tekst: Arrange skirmishing chaff behind your fighting block, extending the formation within coherency so a retreat carries the block through and beyond it. Arrange the chaff across the pursuers' path so they encounter it instead of running directly into the block.
lessen.waarom: He explains that a retreating unit must keep moving until it clears friendly models, letting the block reach safety behind the chaff and then reform or attempt to rally.
lessen.voorbeeld: In his example, Harpies were positioned so even a three-inch retreat would carry his block behind them. A pursuing enemy would encounter the skirmishers at an angle that did not lead directly into the block.
lessen.wanneerNiet: He reports that he later retreated through his unit but failed his rally roll of eight after losing his ranks.

lessen.titel: Position chaff behind enemies to maximise peril tests
lessen.tekst: Position skirmishing chaff behind enemy units you expect to break, arranging the models within coherency to maximise peril tests when enemies flee through them.
lessen.waarom: He says this adds wounds to fleeing enemy units.
lessen.voorbeeld: His ambushing Ungor moved five inches onto the board, with the models behind the front arranged in a three-by-three grid. Either enemy unit would flee through them if he broke it.

lessen.titel: Use chaff to extend enemy retreats towards the board edge
lessen.tekst: Place chaff behind enemy units so a fleeing enemy must keep moving until it clears the chaff, potentially leaving the board. Use an extended skirmishing formation, or bring ambushers on in marching column, to create this flee path.
lessen.waarom: He explains that fleeing through enemy models extends the retreat until the unit is no longer overlapping them. Even if it stays on the board, it may end up too far away to threaten his block.
lessen.voorbeeld: In his example, only about three inches remained behind the Ungor, giving fleeing enemies a chance of being pushed off the board entirely.

lessen.tekst: Use Harpies to get behind enemies for engineered flee paths or peril tests, or behind friendly units to provide a safe path for falling back in good order. He recommends their flying movement for reaching these positions without needing ambush.
lessen.waarom: He values five Harpies at 55 points and their 20-inch flying march, which he says does not require a march-block test.

lessen.titel: Move into realistic charge range for next turn
lessen.tekst: Position your units this turn so they have a realistic charge next turn. Check the actual distance instead of leaving a gap that requires a high roll to close.
lessen.waarom: He explains that a unit's opportunity to fight next turn depends on where it finishes this turn; an average charge distance cannot bridge a larger gap.
lessen.voorbeeld: He contrasts placing a Movement 4 infantry block seven inches from the enemy with leaving it ten inches away: the former creates a realistic threat, while the latter requires a high roll.

bronnen.citaat: The movement phase is where you create your threat ranges for the following turn.

extraCitaten.citaat: You have created a realistic charge threat for next turn.

lessen.titel: Check your angles when moving into charge range
lessen.tekst: When moving closer to the enemy, consider your facing as well as the distance. Avoid creating your own charge opportunity at the cost of exposing your flank to an enemy charge.
lessen.waarom: He stresses that moving into charge range creates opportunities for both players; a poor angle can give the opponent the fight they wanted.
lessen.voorbeeld: He describes a unit approaching enemy cavalry at an incorrect angle: it appears to have a good charge available but has also exposed its flank.
lessen.wanneerNiet: He notes that manoeuvring out of enemy charge arcs becomes much more complicated with more units on the board.

measuring charge arcs and getting out of them is a huge part of

lessen.titel: Time supporting units to join the same combat
lessen.tekst: Move your main unit and its support into position over the preceding one or two turns so they arrive together. Aim to engage the front with one unit while another reaches the flank or rear.

lessen.tekst: Use mobile harassment infantry on a flank near terrain to delay or kill opposing units. If it gets into trouble, march it into cover and out of line of sight to preserve its points.

lessen.waarom: He says an overrun can take the enemy away from the protected unit, while restraining and reforming essentially wastes a turn during which you can shoot and improve your position.
lessen.voorbeeld: In the example he shows, Giant Rats in marching column block Inner Circle Knights' view of Clanrats. The knights must charge the rats, and an overrun would miss the Clanrats, potentially leaving the knights exposed to another round of gunfire.

bronnen.citaat: giant rats here are incredible against first charge units

extraCitaten.citaat: stop a first charge as well.

lessen.titel: Position decoys to draw enemies into countercharges
lessen.tekst: Position a decoy so that charging it takes the enemy into a bad position and sets up your own countercharge. Do not simply push it into the middle of the battlefield and hope for the best.
lessen.waarom: He explains that fleeing bait can draw the enemy forward when no alternative charge target is available. A sacrificial screen can also leave the enemy exposed, whether it restrains or makes an overrun that falls short of the supporting unit.
lessen.voorbeeld: He shows Ellyrian Reavers fleeing through supporting Silver Helms so the advancing chariots can be charged next turn. In another setup, the Reavers stand an inch in front of the chariots, with the Silver Helms far enough away that reaching them by overrun is unlikely but their own charge remains achievable.
lessen.wanneerNiet: He warns that fleeing through the supporting unit causes a panic test and requires the fleeing unit to rally. In the sacrificial-screen setup, a high overrun could reach the support, and the supporting unit could roll too low for its charge.

bronnen.citaat: if they charge them they're going into a bad position.
having your skirmishing chaff unit move up in front and then flee
that meant that my forsaken then had time to hit this unit in the side

lessen.titel: Consider a Tomb Scorpion as dangerous chaff
lessen.tekst: He considers the Tomb Scorpion probably the best chaff unit in the game because its killing threat makes it impossible to ignore.
lessen.waarom: He says it can kill a Pegasus Lord, and even a dragon if it somehow gets to strike first.

bronnen.citaat: scorpion is probably the best chaff unit in the game.

extraCitaten.citaat: you can't ignore it.

lessen.titel: Put vulnerable scorers on Encirclement's protected flank
lessen.tekst: In Encirclement with three strategic objectives, put your more vulnerable scoring unit on the flank where the opponent cannot deploy.
lessen.waarom: He expects the middle objective to be contested and sees the flank without enemy deployment as the safer place for a vulnerable unit.
lessen.voorbeeld: He plans to place his Infernal Guard on that wing to shoot towards the objective and slowly advance if the opponent gives it up.

slowly move towards it if he gives up on it

lessen.titel: Identify how the enemy army intends to win
lessen.tekst: Before choosing your matchups, identify the enemy units' broad roles and how they work together to win. At an event, use that big picture rather than trying to analyse every possible detail.
lessen.waarom: He says time is limited at events, especially when meeting an unfamiliar opponent and trying to be sociable.
lessen.voorbeeld: He expects the two enemy dragons and the Chaos Knights to combine attacks against one unit, break it through damage, then pursue or reform towards the next block.

bronnen.citaat: you need to think about how he's going to win

extraCitaten.citaat: more in terms of big picture heruristics rather than every [clears throat] little detail

lessen.titel: Clear enemy diverters early with light shooting
lessen.tekst: Use light shooting to remove enemy diverters early, rather than leaving them free to control the main combats.

lessen.voorbeeld: In this matchup he redirects his Sneaky Gits from backline troublemaking towards shooting Warhounds, and separates his Hobgoblin Khan from the riders so it can move and shoot at the diverters too.

bronnen.citaat: best to try to go after these war hounds early

lessen.titel: Consider a Wyvern against an unbuffed Warpfire Dragon
lessen.tekst: In this matchup, he favours sending his Warboss on a Wyvern against the Warpfire Dragon when it has not gained the ward save from its spell.
lessen.waarom: He notes that his Wyvern rider has no magical attacks and says that, in his experience, this matchup can be won fairly easily.
lessen.wanneerNiet: His recommendation depends on the Warpfire Dragon not having that ward save active.

lessen.titel: Hide artillery to waste an enemy hunter's time
lessen.tekst: Consider hiding a war machine during deployment and making an enemy come to it, wasting time on the approach.

lessen.titel: Use a central Iron Daemon to bait the dragon
lessen.tekst: In this matchup, deploy the Iron Daemon centrally to tempt the enemy dragon towards it while it shoots without moving.
lessen.waarom: He identifies toughness seven as his advantage and says the opponent cannot do much to kill his Iron Daemon.

lessen.titel: Use fleeing diverters to steer enemy charges
lessen.tekst: Angle a diverter to draw charging enemies towards your waiting units, even if the diverter flees. The speaker recommends this to bring a more aggressive army towards your slower units.
lessen.waarom: He explains that the charger pivots towards the diverter's position and continues in that direction after the diverter flees.
lessen.voorbeeld: His Wolf Riders fled when both the knights and Marauders charged them. Both enemy units came forward angled towards the area where his counterchargers were waiting.
lessen.wanneerNiet: He describes fleeing as a high-stakes choice: his earlier attempts sometimes ended with the fleeing unit being run down.

lessen.titel: Declare terror charges early when fleeing benefits you
lessen.tekst: Consider declaring your terror-causing charges earlier when an enemy fleeing would benefit you. Use the immediate terror test to gain information before making later charge decisions.
lessen.waarom: He says the immediate test lets you move ahead in the charge sequence and see more information before deciding what to do next.
lessen.wanneerNiet: He says this did not apply to the charges in his example: both dragons caused terror, and his Iron Daemon had not been given Hellbound.

bronnen.citaat: think about doing your terror charges earlier if the fleeing is beneficial for you.

extraCitaten.citaat: it allows you to jump up in that order

bronnen.citaat: you can just declare a terror charge and see what will happen next.

lessen.titel: Charge enemy backstops to deny protected retreats
lessen.tekst: If an enemy support unit would protect another unit's fall back in good order, consider charging that support unit separately rather than adding another charger to the main fight.
lessen.waarom: He wanted to prevent the wolves behind the knights from protecting the knights' fall back in good order.
lessen.voorbeeld: He positioned a Bull Centaur to charge the wolves behind the knights, using its all-round charge movement instead of initially charging the knights themselves.

lessen.titel: Clear fleeing blockers before catching the valuable target
lessen.tekst: When fleeing enemies obstruct a charge at a more valuable fleeing unit, look for a legal redirection that lets one charger remove the blocker first. Then resolve the charger that can reach the valuable target.
lessen.waarom: He explains that contacting the fleeing warhounds on the way to the knights would have stopped his charger; the warhounds would not flee again to clear the route.
lessen.voorbeeld: He redirected his Wyvern into the fleeing warhounds and removed them first. His Bull Centaur then redirected into the knights and caught them.
lessen.wanneerNiet: The redirections had to be legal and required successful tests. He says neither the Black Orcs nor the Iron Daemon had a legal alternative charge in this position.

bronnen.citaat: redirect them into the war hounds, hoping to clear them out of the way.

extraCitaten.citaat: make contact with the war hounds, they're not going to flee again.
Instead of charging the wolves, it's closer to the knights.

lessen.titel: Move the charger you need further forward first
lessen.tekst: When two chargers will pivot into each other's paths, decide which one you most need further forward and move it first. Consider their positions after the charge sequence, including access to objectives.
lessen.waarom: He warns that the other unit can hit the first unit's rear and stop, even if it rolled a much longer move.
lessen.voorbeeld: After the knights fled, he moved the Black Orcs first because they could score and needed to be nearer the central objective. The Iron Daemon then hit their rear and stopped.

extraCitaten.citaat: I need those black orcs who can score in this to be closer

lessen.titel: Value high leadership for redirection and restraint
lessen.tekst: Value high leadership when your plan relies on redirecting charges or restraining and reforming. The speaker stresses that testing on leadership eight is much less reliable than testing on ten.
lessen.waarom: He says failed redirections would have left him in a much worse position on the following turn, with the knights able to rally. Reliable restraint and reform also offer substantial advantages in his view.
lessen.voorbeeld: His Sorcerer-Prophet on a large target stayed close to the other units and provided leadership ten. He says many of his tests were automatic in this game.
lessen.wanneerNiet: He warns that a Leadership 8 Archmage will not pass every restraint-and-reform test.

bronnen.citaat: High leadership matters a lot for redirection

extraCitaten.citaat: If you can roll on a high leadership there

bronnen.citaat: you really need to have that leadership as high as possible

lessen.titel: Use superior speed to deploy further back
lessen.tekst: If your army is faster than the opponent's, give yourself more distance instead of automatically deploying on the forward deployment line. Use that speed to open up the battlefield or a flank and delay being caught.
lessen.waarom: He says a fast army has more freedom to play defensively because it can cover more ground than its opponent.

bronnen.citaat: if you're faster than your opponent, you can give yourself a bit more range

extraCitaten.citaat: open up a flank, and not let your opponent catch you for longer.

lessen.titel: Deploy Glade Riders for shooting and a safe withdrawal
lessen.tekst: Hide Glade Riders during deployment and leave enough distance to move out, shoot and Reserve Move back to safety.
lessen.waarom: He highlights their exceptional speed and manoeuvrability.
lessen.voorbeeld: Against Dwarfs, he deployed his Glade Riders on a protected flank, far enough away to move in, shoot and move back to safety.

bronnen.citaat: hide them. Turn one, poke your head out, shoot, reserve, move back.

lessen.titel: Deploy cannons behind Outriders that can Vanguard clear

lessen.titel: Combine your extra forest with an existing forest

lessen.tekst: Position chaff within eight inches to force enemy march tests, and block lanes that enemy units would otherwise march through.

lessen.titel: Use Kiknik and Wolf Riders to hunt Cathayan artillery
lessen.tekst: He recommends Kiknik Toofsnatcha with skirmishing Goblin Wolf Riders to reach and clear Cathayan artillery. Bring enough combat power to kill the Ogre Loader rather than expecting ordinary light cavalry to sweep the crew aside.
lessen.waarom: He found their movement, Reserve Move and skirmishing made them extremely mobile. Kiknik killed an Ogre Loader each turn while the wolves killed the crew; he thinks cannon fire against such light skirmishers may feel wasteful to the opponent.
lessen.voorbeeld: His riders charged on turn two, cleared the cannons and killed the remaining Fire Rain Rocket Battery around turn four or five.
lessen.wanneerNiet: He does not think Glade Riders alone would necessarily do the same job, because the Ogre Loader makes Cathayan artillery harder to clear than ordinary crews.

extraCitaten.citaat: Kicknick killed an ogre a return and the wolves cleaned up the crew.

bronnen.citaat: So, I should be able to wipe out one piece of artillery at a time.

lessen.tekst: For his artillery-hunting plan, he preferred deploying Kiknik's Wolf Riders normally and taking them around the forest. This offered a turn-two charge rather than a turn-three charge after a successful ambush roll.

bronnen.citaat: The night goblins here I wanted to deploy centrally because the fanatics were so important.

lessen.waarom: He values its 18-inch range, achievable casting roll and high armour piercing. As a signature spell that a level-one caster can use, it also allows multiple casters to bring the same spell.
lessen.wanneerNiet: He thinks Tzeentch blaster armies are probably weaker than before because Pillar of Fire is no longer as good.

bronnen.citaat: I think it should come back.

extraCitaten.citaat: The high AP is a really big deal.

lessen.titel: Consider Ruby Ring on eligible unit champions
lessen.tekst: He particularly rates putting Ruby Ring on a unit champion who can take 50-point magic items.
lessen.waarom: He values being able to obtain Fireball through the ring, its 24-inch range and its Strength 4 damage, especially against Toughness 3 targets.
lessen.voorbeeld: He singles out putting the ring on Sisters of Avelorn as an excellent option.

lessen.titel: Manage missile threats instead of trusting failed casts
lessen.tekst: Do not leave vulnerable units exposed to a magic missile simply because its casting or dispelling odds might save them. He recommends managing the threat even when the spell is not reliable.
lessen.waarom: He says good players mitigate losses and manage the odds rather than relying on the missile not going off.
lessen.voorbeeld: He describes the threat to Hexwraiths: merely being within magic missile range can put the whole unit at risk.

bronnen.citaat: They tend to mitigate their losses and manage those odds.

lessen.titel: Use Wind Blast to make enemy charges harder
lessen.tekst: Use Wind Blast's Give Ground effect to push an enemy back and reduce its effective charge reach. He values turning an apparently manageable charge into a difficult one.
lessen.waarom: He describes the pushback as effectively a two-inch movement penalty.
lessen.wanneerNiet: He says access to Wind Blast is often unreliable because other items compete with Lore Familiar, leaving you to roll for the spell.

lessen.titel: Push enemies back from contested objectives with Wind Blast
lessen.tekst: Consider Wind Blast when pushing an enemy back two inches would leave your unit closest to an objective. He thinks that small displacement can decide a closely contested objective.
lessen.waarom: He says games with central or secondary objectives often end with two units still nearby, making a small difference in distance important.
lessen.wanneerNiet: He notes that you will not reliably have Wind Blast every game if you are rolling for spells.

lessen.waarom: He warns that otherwise a hammer can be led around the board or miss intended combats because it no longer has line of sight to the targets it wants to charge.

extraCitaten.citaat: you're going to end up being led around the board

lessen.titel: Compare both armies' ranges before deploying defensively
lessen.tekst: Know how far your own army can move and shoot, and compare its shooting range with the enemy's, including magic missiles. Check enemy charge distances and whether their chargers have Swiftstride.
lessen.waarom: He says that without knowing enemy charge ranges, you will struggle to deploy to avoid those threats or whittle them down before they reach you.

bronnen.citaat: how far you can move uh how far you can shoot

lessen.titel: Deploy as though you will go second
lessen.tekst: When the first turn is still unknown, deploy defensively as though the opponent will act first. Protect the important parts of your army and leave few worthwhile opening targets.
lessen.waarom: He has been caught out too often by losing the first turn. He says that knowing he would go first would let him deploy more aggressively and remove threats before they could return fire.
lessen.voorbeeld: Against High Elves, he hid most of his army and left only a few shooting targets. His important units survived the opening turn, then moved out to remove an archer unit and a bolt thrower.
lessen.wanneerNiet: He says he could deploy much more aggressively if he knew he was going first.

bronnen.citaat: not knowing that means that I have to take the defensive deployment stance

extraCitaten.citaat: he only has a few targets to shoot at
I was able to move out wipe out one of these units

lessen.titel: Deploy beyond enemy movement plus shooting range
lessen.tekst: To avoid opening shooting losses, deploy far enough away that enemy shooters cannot reach you even after moving. Measure their movement and shooting reach together.
lessen.waarom: He wants to avoid taking losses before his own first turn.
lessen.voorbeeld: He deployed his Glade Riders beyond the Outriders' combined movement and shooting reach. If he went second they could not move and shoot him; if he went first he could move up and shoot them.

bronnen.citaat: whatever their movement is plus their shooting range

extraCitaten.citaat: so that if I go second he can't move and shoot them

lessen.titel: Clear fast and ranged threats with Wood Elves
lessen.tekst: With Wood Elves, prioritise removing the enemy's fast and ranged threats. Use that clearance to bring your mobility advantage into play against the remaining army.
lessen.waarom: He says even enemy dogs can kill his Toughness 3 troops. Against the infantry-heavy High Elf army, removing ranged threats made his mobility the biggest factor in the game.
lessen.voorbeeld: Against High Elves, his protected army moved out after the opening turn and removed an archer unit and a bolt thrower. He believes this defensive deployment gave him the advantage by about turn two.
lessen.wanneerNiet: He wanted to remove the Skin Wolves early, but found that difficult because they were quick and reached combat, where he struggled to shoot them.

bronnen.citaat: clear the fast and the ranged threats

extraCitaten.citaat: my Mobility becomes the biggest factor in the game
skin wolves I would have loved to deal with early

lessen.waarom: He finds that rolling five spells and replacing the poor results prevents a bad spell selection.
lessen.voorbeeld: He replaces Steed of Shadows because his list has no infantry, and sometimes replaces another spell when it is not needed for the matchup. He has taken Fleshy Abundance, Blue Fire and The Summoning through these swaps.

lessen.titel: Consider a steed for the Chaos Lord's all-round charges
lessen.tekst: Against Bretonnian Pegasus Knights and evasive Wood Elves, he chooses a steed rather than a Daemonic Mount for his Chaos Lord. He wants the Lord to leave his unit and threaten charges in any direction.

lessen.titel: Use a Gigantic Spawn to pin enemies for support
lessen.tekst: He uses a Gigantic Spawn of Chaos as a tarpit, pinning enemy units so the rest of his force can join the fight. After trying two, he found one enough for his list.

lessen.titel: Combo-charge the poison block with as many units as possible
lessen.tekst: He considers a coordinated charge with as many units as possible in the same turn the best, and in his view only, way to defeat this poison Death Star. Commit enough force to keep winning combats and grind the block down.
lessen.waarom: He explains that the skeletons can be surprisingly difficult to hit because of their stacked abilities and spells. The block also inflicts substantial damage in return while he grinds it down.
lessen.voorbeeld: His Chaos Knights and surviving Dragon Ogres were among the units that charged James's block on turn two, before several turns of grinding combat.

lessen.titel: Reach the poison block early enough to grind it down
lessen.tekst: Against this poison Death Star, engage as soon as you can with as many of your grinding units surviving as possible. Do not spend several turns hesitating or dancing around it before committing.
lessen.waarom: He warns that the block can delete or cripple a unit each turn. He also says a late engagement may leave too few combat rounds to grind through it.

lessen.voorbeeld: He directed all his Dragon Ogres' attacks at the Illusion priest rather than the other character they could attack. Killing that priest removed Glittering Robe from the fight.

lessen.titel: Stack buffs rather than seek fair fights
lessen.tekst: Avoid fair fights when you can and try to overwhelm the opponent. Stack as many buffs as you can on the attacking unit without taking too much risk, so a little bad luck does not ruin the attack.
lessen.waarom: He says this stacks the odds in your favour even though you cannot control the dice.

lessen.titel: Make advancing casters choose between charging and conveyance magic
lessen.tekst: Position chaff so that an advancing casting unit must charge it to continue forward, at the cost of casting its conveyance spell. The speaker praises this as a way to delay that unit.
lessen.waarom: He explains that declaring the charge would prevent Walk Between Worlds, while the Outriders' Fire and Flee and Swiftstride made catching them unlikely.
lessen.voorbeeld: His opponent's Outriders shot at his Phoenix Guard while obstructing his Lothern Sea Guard's advance. He cast Walk Between Worlds and removed the Outriders with unusually successful shooting, but his Sea Guard stayed further back than he wanted, buying time for his opponent to improve his position and keep his Sorcerers active.

lessen.titel: Zone enemies with overlapping threats
lessen.tekst: Use your pieces' threat ranges to restrict the opponent's choices without committing to an attack. Look for positions where a piece can threaten a charge while also contesting enemy magic.
lessen.waarom: He says putting the opponent in two minds gives them more opportunities to make mistakes or roll poorly.

lessen.tekst: When deploying along the sideline, angle units slightly towards the centre. Leave room to wheel inward if the opponent does not deploy opposite them.

lessen.titel: Bait with a Razorgor and follow with a Tuskgor Chariot

lessen.titel: Contain mobile enemies with threats from opposite directions
lessen.tekst: When trying to contain mobile enemy units, approach from opposite sides while another threat keeps the same enemy units in its charge arc. Coordinate these threats to stop the enemy simply slipping away sideways.
lessen.waarom: He needed to reach the units sheltering behind terrain while also keeping them there. He found that the Star Dragon exerted significant influence even without fighting, because the enemy avoided it and took chances against his other units instead.
lessen.voorbeeld: His Skycutter attacked from the left, his Dragon Princes approached from the opposite side, and his Star Dragon threatened the group. He says the coordinated effort let the Skycutter tear through three units.

lessen.titel: Angle side attackers towards the boundary to cover escapes

lessen.waarom: He says this herds enemies towards the back boundary, which they cannot cross without being lost, while keeping their escape routes covered by another unit's charge arc.

lessen.wanneerNiet: He notes that ambushers cannot charge on the turn they arrive, and their arrival depends on a roll until round five. His Glade Riders failed to arrive on turns two and three, when they could at least have distracted the enemy or caused some shooting damage.

bronnen.citaat: using this unit as a flank or rear support charger.

extraCitaten.citaat: you can bring them on in an area that's protected
They're there to just be a utility piece and assist.

lessen.titel: Make the enemy spread out to open ambush space
lessen.tekst: When planning an ambush against a tightly grouped enemy, make it move and spread out to create useful entry space for your ambushers.
lessen.waarom: He found the closely grouped Dwarfs initially left only limited entry pockets, one of which was blocked by a large rock. As they dispersed and changed facing, useful space opened for his Glade Riders.
lessen.voorbeeld: In his Wood Elf game against Dwarfs, his Wild Riders advanced down the right flank and his dragon fought through the middle and backline. The Dwarf formation spread out as the game developed, opening a beneficial arrival area for his Glade Riders.

bronnen.citaat: make them move, so there's space for my glade riders to come on.

extraCitaten.citaat: he's already started to disperse

lessen.titel: Consider Close Order Wolf Riders for ambush support
lessen.tekst: He wants to explore ambushing with Close Order Goblin Wolf Riders in the Nomadic army. With a banner, he sees five of them rear-charging as a way to bring four static combat resolution into a fight.
lessen.waarom: He thinks static combat resolution arriving behind the opponent is valuable. He also recalls fights where his attacks against war machines failed and thinks two combat resolution would probably be enough to break them.
lessen.wanneerNiet: He presents this as something he intends to explore once his Orcs and Goblins are painted, rather than a combination he has demonstrated in this game.

bronnen.citaat: those wolf riders can be close order, which is a big deal.

extraCitaten.citaat: That's four static combat ress from five wolf riders with a banner.
static combat res arriving on your opponent's back end is very valuable
